title: Canary Rollout Visual Composer for Private Clusters with Network Dependency Overlays
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Create a visual composer inside the Private Console that allows SREs and platform engineers to define, preview, and run canary/ phased rollouts across private clusters while visualizing network dependencies and potential impact surface (tenants, routes, egress paths).

Context: Private deployments often have complex networking (VPC peering, NAT/GW, internal load balancers) and multi-tenant clusters. Rollouts (canary, canary+fade, A/B) need to show where traffic will be shifted, which tenant subnets are affected, and what path/egress changes may occur so operators can make informed tradeoffs without jumping between the rollout UI and network topology views.

Primary users: Platform engineers, SREs, Solutions Engineers for on-prem customers. Secondary: Customer success during onboarding.

Key UX goals:
- Surface network dependency overlays on rollout timelines and cluster maps.
- Provide an intuitive composer to build phased rollouts using drag-to-schedule lanes (percent traffic, duration, add rollback step).
- Simulate downstream impact: list of tenants affected, estimated latency delta (coarse), and potential egress cost flags.
- Inline safety checks and automatic suggestions (e.g., require drain on nodes with active KV cache, warn if cross-region peering will be hit).
- Exportable rollout plan and snapshot for audit logs and support handoff.

Scope / Deliverables:
- High-fidelity Figma prototype for composer + map overlays (desktop).
- Compact mobile/compact layout for on-call view.
- Interaction spec for rollout state machine (start, pause, rollback, emergency abort).
- Accessibility pass: keyboard-first composer interactions and aria labels for overlay elements.
- Acceptance criteria and observability hooks for engineering to emit rollout metrics (percent complete, step latency, rollback reason).

User stories:
- As an SRE, I can visually place a canary step on a cluster map and see which tenant subnets will receive traffic so I can avoid sensitive networks.
- As a platform engineer, I can add a conditional pause (auto-pause if 95th latency increases > X) and preview how network overlays change during that step.
- As a support engineer, I can export the rollout snapshot with linked network paths to include in a support ticket.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Composer allows 3-step rollout with percent controls and durations and persists as a named plan.
2) Network overlay toggles on/off; when on, it highlights at-risk subnets and enumerates tenant IDs.
3) Simulate button shows estimated impacted tenants and a confidence note for latency/cost estimates.
4) Export generates a JSON snapshot and a human-readable PDF for audits.
5) Keyboard navigation covers primary composer functions and overlay toggles; test with VoiceOver/JAWS.

Risks & open questions:
- Latency/cost estimates require backend heuristics; we need an API contract from Eng for acceptable flat confidence bands.
- How to represent cross-region failover when clusters span private locations — design will provide a compact summary and link to full topology.
- Security implications of visualizing tenant IDs — may require redaction or role-based reveal.

Metrics to evaluate success:
- Time to create a rollout plan (target < 8 minutes for first run).
- Reduction in support tickets caused by network misconfiguration during rollouts (target -30% in trial cohort).
- Adoption: percent of Dedicated customers using composer for at least one rollout within 30 days.

Deliverables to hand off to Eng:
- Figma prototype with redlines and interaction flows.
- Interaction spec (keyboard, ARIA, animation thresholds).
- Edge cases doc: overlapping rollouts, missing network metadata, degraded cluster visibility.

Notes: We'll coordinate with ENG to fetch tenant mapping APIs and with PM to determine the export schema for audits (legal/compliance requirement in some enterprise contracts).
